items.q: What do interviewers expect at ~4 YOE that they don't expect from a junior?
items.a: Trade-off reasoning, production debugging stories with metrics, ownership of API+DB+auth+observability end-to-end, and mentoring/communication — not just CRUD syntax.

items.q: How would you structure 2 weeks of prep before a mid-senior .NET interview?
items.a: Week 1: async, DI, ASP.NET pipeline, EF/SQL (N+1, indexes, isolation). Week 2: security, messaging, caching, observability, three system designs, and STAR/resume drills. Daily: 30–45 min flashcards + one design sketch.

items.q: IEnumerable vs IQueryable — when does each execute?
items.a: IEnumerable operators run in-process when enumerated. IQueryable builds an expression tree; the provider (EF) translates to SQL when enumerated/materialized (ToList, First, etc.). Mixing them poorly can pull too much data into memory.

items.q: When would you use Span<T> and what are its limits?
items.a: Use Span for slicing/parsing contiguous memory without allocations. Limits: ref struct — can't be stored on the heap, can't be class fields, can't be used across await. Use Memory<T> when you need to hold the view longer.

items.q: Why can .Result deadlock, and how do you fix it?
items.a: If a SynchronizationContext must resume the continuation but the thread is blocked waiting for the task, you deadlock. Fix: async all the way with await; never block in UI/legacy sync contexts. In ASP.NET Core prefer await over Result always.

items.q: When is ValueTask appropriate?
items.a: When a method frequently completes synchronously and allocation of Task shows up in profiles. Rules: await at most once, don't store/reuse casually, convert with AsTask() only when needed (allocates).

items.q: Why can't you inject DbContext into a Singleton?
items.a: DbContext is scoped. Captured by a singleton it lives for the app lifetime, becoming shared/unsafe across requests (threading + disposed state). Create a scope per unit of work via IServiceScopeFactory.

items.q: Why is IHttpClientFactory preferred?
items.a: It manages handler lifetimes and DNS refresh, avoiding socket exhaustion from disposing HttpClient too often or holding one forever. Enables named/typed clients and resilience policies.

items.q: Describe the ASP.NET Core request pipeline.
items.a: Kestrel accepts the connection and parses HTTP, then invokes the middleware pipeline in order. Routing selects an endpoint; the handler runs; the response flows back through middleware. Auth middleware must be placed correctly relative to UseRouting/UseEndpoints.

items.q: Minimal APIs vs Controllers — when do you choose each?
items.a: Minimal for small/focused APIs and fast delivery. Controllers for larger apps needing conventions, filters, inheritance, and clearer organization. Either can be production-grade; choose for maintainability of the team.

items.q: How do you make POST /orders safe under client retries?
items.a: Require an Idempotency-Key header. Persist key → response (or request hash). On replay, return the original result instead of creating a second order. Combine with unique constraints for defense in depth.

items.q: When would you pick gRPC over REST?
items.a: Internal service-to-service calls needing strong contracts, binary efficiency, and streaming. Prefer REST for public HTTP APIs, browser clients, and HTTP caching.

items.q: What is the N+1 problem and how do you fix it in EF?
items.a: Loading a collection then lazy-loading a navigation per row causes 1+N queries. Fix with Include/ThenInclude, Select projections, AsSplitQuery for big graphs, or explicit SQL joins. Verify with logging or a profiler.

items.q: When do you use AsNoTracking?
items.a: Read-only queries where you won't Update/SaveChanges. Skipping tracking reduces memory and CPU. Don't use it if you need to mutate and persist the same instances.

items.q: What does READ COMMITTED SNAPSHOT buy you?
items.a: Row versioning so readers don't take shared locks that block writers (and vice versa) for typical read committed scenarios. Trade-off: tempdb version store cost and different anomaly profile — know it isn't full serializability.

items.q: How do you handle optimistic concurrency in EF Core?
items.a: Add a RowVersion/timestamp (or token) configured as concurrency token. On SaveChanges conflict, catch DbUpdateConcurrencyException, reload database values, merge or ask the user, retry.

items.q: Explain Authorization Code flow with PKCE.
items.a: Client sends authorize request with code_challenge; user authenticates; AS returns a code; client exchanges code + code_verifier for tokens. PKCE stops intercepted codes from being redeemed by attackers who lack the verifier.

items.q: Name five OWASP mitigations you'd apply to an ASP.NET API.
items.a: Parameterized queries/EF; output encoding; CSRF protection for cookie sessions; secrets out of source; least-privilege authZ policies; strict DTOs; security headers; dependency scanning.

items.q: When do you choose Kafka over RabbitMQ?
items.a: High-throughput event streams, replay/retention, partition-scaled consumers, and log-oriented processing. Choose RabbitMQ for complex routing, classic work queues, and lower operational complexity at moderate volume.

items.q: What problem does the outbox pattern solve?
items.a: Dual-write: updating DB and publishing a message separately can lose one side on failure. Outbox writes the event in the same DB transaction; a process publishes later, yielding reliable at-least-once delivery with idempotent consumers.

items.q: How do you debug increasing API latency over days?
items.a: Check metrics (P95, errors, dependency times), distributed traces for slow spans, runtime counters (thread pool queue, GC), recent deploys/config, and classics: N+1, missing index, sync-over-async, cache stampede, chatty logging.

items.q: When should a retry policy NOT retry?
items.a: On non-transient errors (400 validation, 401/403), non-idempotent POSTs without idempotency keys, and after a circuit is open. Retry timeouts/5xx/connection resets with jittered backoff.

items.q: When are microservices the wrong choice?
items.a: Small team/domain, unclear boundaries, or when a modular monolith would ship faster with fewer failure modes. Microservices add network latency, consistency, and ops cost — justify with real scaling or team ownership needs.

items.q: Describe cache-aside and one failure mode.
items.a: App reads cache; on miss, loads DB and populates cache with TTL. Failure modes: stampedes on expiry, stale reads after writes without invalidation, and caching personalized/security-sensitive data incorrectly.

items.q: App Service vs AKS for a single .NET API?
items.a: Default to App Service for one API needing speed-to-prod and managed scaling. Choose AKS when you run many services, need custom networking/sidecars, or already operate Kubernetes. Don't adopt K8s for resume points alone.

items.q: Outline a notification service for email/SMS/push.
items.a: API accepts notify requests with idempotency keys; persist outbox; workers per channel with retries/DLQ; template service; user preferences; provider adapters; metrics on send success/latency; never block the upstream order flow on provider latency.

items.q: Give a STAR story structure for a production incident.
items.a: Situation: symptom + blast radius. Task: your ownership. Action: how you diagnosed (metrics/traces), mitigated, fixed root cause. Result: MTTR, error rate drop, follow-up (test, alert, postmortem).
